title: How Blake Anderson built RizzGPT, Umax and Cal AI into $10M with influencers and AI
summary: Whop profile of Blake Anderson, who built consumer AI apps (RizzGPT, Umax, Cal AI) with no coding background and grew them mainly through influencer marketing. His quoted interview covers channel mix, app longevity, thinking long-term, and funding Apex at a loss. Much of the essay is the writer's context; only his quotes are used here.

principles.text: Run every channel, but treat influencers as the most profitable acquisition strategy for consumer apps.
principles.quote: We also engage in internal UGC. We do paid platform ads, so Meta, TikTok, that sort of thing. So everything, but influencers are our most profitable strategy.

principles.text: Consumer apps with working distribution keep earning long after launch instead of fading out.
principles.quote: as you can see, they don't just die. RizzGPT is still doing 200(k) a month.

principles.text: Don't chase a revenue number; optimize for long-term impact and fund it with resources.
principles.quote: I don't think about business in regards to how can I make $10 million. I think about it in regards to how I can maximize my impact in the footprint that I leave on the world.

principles.text: Short-term money thinking is a mistake; get the resources needed to build the long-term vision.
principles.quote: It's nonsensical to think about money in the short term. You just need to think about how you can get the necessary resources to build out the long-term vision.

principles.text: Give co-founders clear ownership of their domains and transfer your hard-won lessons to them fast.
principles.quote: We each have our primary domains within the company and the processes and stacks in which we own. I've learned lessons over my time in entrepreneurship and I just want to be able to transfer them to my co-founders as quickly and efficiently as possible.

principles.text: Accept extreme risk and bet big rather than play safe, even at a real chance of failure.
principles.quote: I would rather live at the extreme with a 50% chance that it all crashes and burns.
